transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, I guess the main thing is I’m just worn down almost all the time. Like, even if I sleep a full night, I still wake up feeling like I’m already behind. And then by the time I get through work and try to deal with the house—there’s always clutter, mail, laundry, random things on the counters—I don’t really have much left in me for anything else.
Do you find yourself enjoying the things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I still do them sometimes, but it’s not the same. Most days there’s this kind of low, gray feeling running in the background. I can go to the lab and talk to people and do what I’m supposed to do, but things don’t really feel light or exciting anymore.

Like baking—I used to actually enjoy planning what to make, and checking on the telescope used to give me this little spark, you know? Now it’s more like… I do it, but I’m not really feeling much from it. And then I’ll get distracted by some random thing, like needing to clean the counter before I can even start, and then the whole thing just feels heavier than it should.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

A little, I guess, but not like before. Baking still sounds nice in theory, and sometimes I’ll check on the telescope, but most days there’s just this low, gray mood in the background. Like I can still go to the lab and talk to people and look normal, but I don’t really feel light or excited about those things anymore.

And then I’ll get sidetracked by something stupid, like a dish in the sink or realizing I forgot to put away flour from the last time, and suddenly it’s not relaxing, it’s just… another thing.
How long have you been feeling this low, gray mood?

Um… I think it’s been a little over two years now. It kind of started not long after we moved into this older house, which sounds silly because the house is fine, it just has all these little things that always need attention—like one drawer sticks, and there’s this weird corner where dust collects no matter what I do.

But yeah, the low, gray feeling… that’s been sort of the baseline since shortly after that move.
Do you often feel worried or anxious about things?

I don’t know… I mean, worried, sure, sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d call it anxious exactly. It’s more like I get caught up in little things, and then my mind sort of wanders off.

Like if something in the house is out of place, I’ll notice it, and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I should fix that first before doing whatever I was actually going to do. But I don’t know if that’s worry or just… me getting stuck on details.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?

Most of the time? I’m not sure. I don’t think I walk around feeling panicky or anything like that. It’s more like… I can get stuck on small things, like I said, and then I’m thinking about that instead of whatever I meant to do.

Like yesterday I noticed the hallway rug was crooked, and then somehow I was thinking about whether the floor under it needs cleaning, and then I’d lost track of what I’d gone upstairs for. But I don’t know if that’s anxiety, exactly. Maybe you mean something different by anxious?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past two years?

I don’t think so? I mean, I haven’t really been tracking it closely. My clothes seem mostly the same, I guess. Sometimes I’ll feel like my jeans are tighter, but then I realize they just came out of the dryer, and that’s its own whole annoying thing because the laundry room is cramped and the vent gets lint everywhere.

But, um… no, I haven’t noticed a big weight change.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge?

Nervous or on edge… I don’t know. Not in a constant way, I don’t think. I mean, I can feel kind of keyed up if there’s a lot happening around me, or if I’m trying to do something and there’s some little thing distracting me.

Like even here, I noticed the chair leg is a little uneven, and then I start thinking about whether it’s the floor or the chair, which is silly, because that’s not what you asked. So… I’m not sure I’d say I often feel nervous. Maybe sometimes, but I don’t really know how to measure that.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now feel completely uninterested in?

Completely uninterested… I don’t know if I’d say completely. I still do things. I go to the lab, I talk to people, I can get through the day.

But most days there’s this kind of low, gray feeling in the background. Like, things I used to look forward to—baking, or checking the telescope, even just seeing what came out right or noticing something interesting—don’t feel as light, I guess. I’ll still think, “Oh, I should make bread,” and then I end up staring at the flour container because the lid never sits right, and then it feels like too much trouble.

So… not totally uninterested, maybe, but the excitement is pretty muted now.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened or things you've done?

Guilty… um, I don’t know. I mean, I’ll replay things sometimes, like if I said something awkward or forgot to respond to an email, but I’m not sure that’s guilt exactly. It’s more like my brain keeps picking at it.

Like last week I spent way too long thinking about whether I’d closed a cabinet in the lab, and then that turned into remembering this whole thing with a drawer that sticks because someone put tape on the runner—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I don’t think I feel guilty a lot, at least not in some big way. I’m not sure.
Are there any activities that you have completely stopped doing because you no longer find them enjoyable?

Completely stopped… yeah, sort of. I mean, I haven’t stopped everything. I’m still getting my lab work done, mostly. But things are slower than they should be—grant drafts, little routine project decisions, those take me much longer now.

At home, though, I’ve kind of stopped keeping up with the things that used to give my evenings shape. Baking, the bonsai, making telescope plans. I’ll think about doing them, and then somehow I don’t. Like the bonsai tools are still in the same place, which bothers me because one of the trays is slightly crooked, but I still don’t actually do anything with them.

So… yes, some things I used to enjoy have just sort of fallen away.
Do you often find yourself worrying about the future?

Yeah… I do, I think. Not in a dramatic way, more like I catch myself assuming things won’t really get back to normal.

Like the house—I keep thinking it’s never going to feel properly settled, which is probably silly because it’s just boxes and little repairs and the one closet door that doesn’t close evenly. But then that turns into, “Well, I’m probably just going to keep functioning at this reduced level,” and then I don’t really plan ahead.

I used to like planning trips or stargazing projects, checking dates and sky conditions and all that, and now I sort of stop before I start because I assume I won’t follow through anyway. So… yes, I guess I do worry about the future, or maybe I expect less from it.
Are there any activities that you've completely lost pleasure in?

Completely lost pleasure… I don’t know if I’d say completely. It’s more like most days there’s this low, gray feeling kind of running in the background.

I can still go to the lab, talk to people, do what I’m supposed to do mostly. But things that used to make me feel lighter—like baking, or checking the telescope, even just looking at the sky conditions—don’t really give me that little spark anymore. I’ll think, “Oh, I should do that,” and then it just feels flat.

Sorry, I’m probably not answering exactly. I wouldn’t say everything is gone, but the excitement is definitely… muted.
Do you often feel overwhelmed by fear or apprehension about everyday situations?

Overwhelmed by fear… I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. Everyday situations can feel like more than they should, but I don’t know that it’s fear exactly.

Like, if there’s a repair person coming by or I have to sort out some house thing, I’ll overthink the timing and whether the hallway is clear enough—actually the hallway still has that stack of boxes I keep meaning to move, which is annoying because it makes the whole place feel unfinished. But I don’t usually feel scared, exactly.

So… apprehensive sometimes, maybe, but not really overwhelmed by fear.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past two years?

I don’t think so. I mean, my clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything.

I haven’t really been tracking it closely, though. The scale is in the bathroom, but it’s sort of wedged near this box of cleaning stuff I still haven’t unpacked, so I don’t step on it much. But no, I don’t think I’ve lost a significant amount over the past couple years.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I’m crying all the time or anything dramatic, but most days there’s this low, gray mood in the background.

I can still go to the lab and talk to people and get through what I need to do. It’s just… things don’t feel light the way they used to. Like baking, or checking on the telescope—actually I used to really look forward to seeing how the sky conditions were, even if it was just routine—and now it’s more like I do it, or think about doing it, and there’s not much feeling there.

So yes, I guess I do feel sad most of the time, in a kind of muted way.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy and find pleasure in?

Some things, maybe a little. I still do them, at least. Baking, sometimes, or checking on the telescope stuff, but it’s not the same kind of pleasure I used to get from it.

Most days there’s just this low, gray mood running in the background. I can go to the lab and talk to people and get through the day, but I don’t really feel light or excited about things. Even with baking—like I’ll think about making something, and then I remember the mixing bowls are in that awkward cabinet, and I should really reorganize it—and by then it just feels like effort instead of fun.

So… I guess I still sort of enjoy a few things, but it’s muted. Not like before.
Do you feel your low, gray mood is mild or more severe most of the time?

I’d say mild, most of the time. It’s not like I can’t function—I still go to the lab, talk to people, get through what I need to do.

It’s more like this low grayness running in the background. Like, I’ll think about baking or checking the telescope, and I know those things used to make me feel kind of interested or happy, but now it’s just… flatter. Not severe exactly, just always sort of there.
Would you say your low, gray mood is affecting your daily life in a moderate or severe way?

Moderate, I guess. Not severe. I’m still getting my lab work done, so from the outside it probably looks mostly fine.

But things take longer than they should. Grant drafts especially—I’ll sit with them open and sort of circle around the same paragraph, or routine project decisions that should be quick feel like… I don’t know, like wading through something.

And at home it shows up more. I used to have these little plans that gave shape to my downtime—baking something on the weekend, working on the bonsai, checking telescope plans or sky conditions—and lately I just don’t keep up with them. I think about it, and then it sort of slips away. So… moderate, probably. Not falling apart, but definitely affected.
Would you say your low, gray mood is interfering with your relationships or daily activities more than it is with your interest in activities?

I think it’s more the daily activities than relationships, if I’m choosing between those. I’m still getting my lab work done, but it’s slower—grant drafts especially, and even routine project decisions take me longer than they should.

And then at home, it kind of shows up in the things that used to structure my downtime. Like baking, the bonsai, telescope plans… I don’t keep up with them the way I used to. Although then I start thinking, maybe that is “interest,” because those are activities I used to enjoy. But it feels less like I don’t care at all and more like everything takes this extra push, and I just don’t follow through.
